Subject: Recurring E34 lockouts and scale from week one on a "descaled" refurb

We bought the refurbished Vantorre CX-10 (s/n VT21-30877) from Kelsall. It was delivered and commissioned at our Fitzroy bistro on 14 September. We paid $14,800 and the warranty runs to March 2027. Here's how the first eight weeks have gone.

On 22 September the tech attended for E34 (steam generator low water level), with intermittent lockouts in combi and steam modes. The service report shows 9 x E34 in the error log since 14/09, which is the day it arrived. The level sensor was replaced under warranty.

On 3 October I reported E34 back 4 times that week. I also flagged the core probe reading low. I tested it against a Thermapen in a lamb shoulder twice: the oven said 63°C and the Thermapen said 70°C both times. That's a 7 degree gap, which matters a lot in a kitchen that cooks to temperature.

On 6 October the steam generator was found "heavily scaled". It was descaled and flushed, the probe was recalibrated, and Kelsall recommended we install a water softener because of hard water.

The water doesn't support that. Our supplier gives Fitzroy's average hardness as about 15 mg/L as CaCO3, which they class as soft, some of the softest in the country. The oven had been on our water for just over three weeks when heavy scale was found. That's hard to square with the listing, which says "steam generator descaled and pressure tested". The error log showing E34 from delivery day points the same way.

On Saturday 24 October, E34 locked us out at 6:10pm with 60 covers booked. We finished the lamb on the stove and in the deck oven and took the pork belly off the menu.

On 27 October there was E34 again and further scale was found. Kelsall has put this down to site water, so it isn't covered under warranty. We've been invoiced a $280 + GST ($308) callout on a six-week-old unit with a parts and labour warranty.

To be fair, the tech has been prompt and easy to deal with every time, and this isn't about him. The issue is the unit's condition on arrival and the seller treating a scale problem on soft water as the customer's fault.

If you're looking at a refurb combi, ask for the error log and a look inside the steam generator before it ships, and check your local water hardness yourself so you have the numbers ready if this happens to you.

reasons: It says the callout has been invoiced, but Brett said it would be invoiced.
